module_name: Social Network Analysis: Centrality, Community Detection, Brokerage
module_description: Module 16 introduces network thinking for social data: graph construction from replies/mentions/follows/co-hashtags, centrality measures (degree, betweenness, eigenvector/PageRank), community detection (Louvain, Leiden, label propagation), brokerage/structural holes, and ego-network analysis. It links metrics to interpretation (who bridges communities) and covers visualization and layout discipline.
core_concepts: Centrality measures and what they actually imply
learning_outcomes: C3 Build a network from a social corpus
C4 Compute and interpret centrality and communities
C5 Relate network structure to substantive claims (echo chamber, bridge accounts)
methods_models: Graph building (igraph/networkx), Louvain/Leiden clustering, betweenness/eigenvector/betweenness-centrality, modularity and conductance, layout algorithms (ForceAtlas)
evaluation_metrics: Modularity, conductance/NMI (when ground truth available), centralization, robustness of communities across resolutions
pitfalls_limitations: Follow graph vs interaction graph conflation, self-loops from retweets/mentions, deleted accounts breaking paths, scale-vs-meaning asymmetry (degree is not influence), over-interpreting single clusters
tools_stack: networkx, igraph, leidenalg, python-igraph, graph-tool (optional), Gephi, R: igraph/ggraph/tidygraph
commercial_platforms: Gephi used for visualization and exploration; commercial tools not needed
tools_access_cost: Free (open-source); large graph compute needs memory
lab_activities: Build a mention/reply network on an issue, compute centralities, run Leiden, and write interpretation of the top bridges
datasets_apis: Reply/mention network from X or Bluesky on a public issue
assessment_methods: Lab notebook plus graph figures and a short interpretation; graded on correctness of metrics and defensibility of substantive claims
data_collection_workflow: Build the interaction graph from collected data -> deduplicate accounts and edges -> compute metrics -> cluster communities -> archive graph object and code
textbooks: Barabasi, Network Science (2016), ch. on centrality/communities
Zafarani et al., Social Media Mining, ch. 4-5
key_papers: 2024-2026 papers on coordinated networks, bridged communities, and network measures on Bluesky
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: Bluesky's open graph made large-scale follow/interaction networks easy to build, renewing SNA in teaching and research
industry_relevance: Used in disinformation/trust-and-safety teams, political-communication research units, community-management analytics, and influence-marketing measurement; network metrics are standard deliverables in crisis-mapping briefings.
localization_context: Practised on Indonesian case networks (election-issue discussion, anti-hoax communities, local brand mentions) where the platform mix and language mix differ from US/EU benchmark datasets.
ethics_regulation: Re-identification risk of pseudonymous accounts, doxxing risk when publishing ego-networks, and the ethical line between mapping influence and surveilling individuals; UU PDP applies to any data tied to identifiable accounts.
case_study_scenarios: Map who bridges the pro and contra camps on a local policy discussion.
deliverable_format: Network object + centrality table + community report + figure
